key_insight: RheOFormer’s failures in Bingham flow prediction can be reduced through logarithmic velocity representations, gradient-aware losses, and a few strategically selected training cases.
engineering_relevance: These remedies support more data-efficient neural surrogates for viscoplastic flow simulation, particularly when low-gradient plug regions challenge prediction accuracy.
method: Evaluate RheOFormer on steady Bingham channel flow across dataset structures, numerical ranges, and input representations.
Introduce logarithmic velocity representations and gradient-aware losses to improve plug-region predictions.
Augment training with selected cases covering missing physical regimes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved accuracy in challenging regimes, reduced extrapolation errors with few added cases, and accurate steady-state prediction from a single partially developed snapshot, outperforming input copying.
watch_item: Validation is limited to a simple channel geometry and Bingham model; generalization to complex geometries and other constitutive laws remains unestablished.
paper_title: Failure Modes and Data-Efficient Remedies for Transformer-Based Prediction of Viscoplastic Flows
